title: Last-point ordinal indexing adjunction
statement:
Use small ordinary nerves, quasicategories and coherent transformations of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a containing universe. Let $\Delta_+$ have objects the finite ordinals $J$, including $\varnothing$, and all monotone maps, and let $\Delta\subset\Delta_+$ contain the nonempty ordinals. Define $D$ to have the same objects as $\Delta_+$ and morphisms $J\to K$ all monotone maps $J\sqcup\{\infty\}\to K\sqcup\{\infty\}$ fixing the new greatest element, composed as maps. Let $i:\Delta\to D$ and $j:\Delta_+\to D$ extend monotone maps to fix the new last element, with no ordinary element sent to it. Let $U:D\to\Delta$ send $J$ to $J\sqcup\{\infty\}$ and each arrow to its underlying monotone map. Then $i\dashv U$, with the natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_D(iA,J)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(A,UJ)$$
given by restriction to $A$, and $\varnothing$ is initial in $D$.

source.place: HTT Lemma 6.1.3.16 (printed p.553), definition of the category of last-point-preserving ordinal maps, and Lemma 6.1.3.17: explicit ordinary indexing adjunction supporting the right shift. No Stacks tag states this indexing assertion.
